Hardware you actually own.

Placeholder copy for the hero. Two lines of positioning, then out of the way.

01 — The device

An edge computer, not a gateway to someone else's cloud.

Runs the workload where the sensors are. Local by default, connected when you choose. The enclosure is printed, the internals are documented, and nothing here phones home unless you tell it to.

95 × 27 × 97 mm · Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W · Debian

02 — Compute

A Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W on a carrier that does the hard parts.

Regulation from 12–24 V, a real-time clock, status LEDs, a button, a buzzer, and the 32-pin cartridge interface. The compute module is the most replaceable thing in the stack — which is rather the point.

Carrier 92.5 × 90 mm · Pi Zero 2 W · in production until at least 2030

03 — Loadout

The application lives on a cartridge.

One 32-pin interface, one board outline, one faceplate envelope. Swap the cartridge and the device becomes a different instrument — without touching the compute, the enclosure, or the software underneath.

04 — Mounting

A dovetail rail down each side.

The same 2.7 mm tongue slides into both walls, so every mount is one printed part in two orientations. Screw it to a wall, clip it to a brick, or leave the rail bare.

05 — Branding

Your device, your label.

Printed in Bambu PETG, with an 85 × 25 mm matt label set into the top face. Upload your own artwork and it ships wearing it.

Finish

06 — Identity

Every unit carries its own name.

A 76.7 × 13 mm recess on the underside takes the assembly label: serial, MAC, batch and claim code. Printed per unit at assembly, not per batch.

Square-cut, 0.25 mm deep, inset 8 mm from both ends.
